stages.name: base
stages.text:
Build an LRU cache simulator.
Input (stdin, one JSON object): {"capacity": int >= 0, "ops": [op, ...]} where op is ["put", key: string, value: int] or ["get", key: string].
get returns the stored value, or null when absent, and marks the key most recently used. put stores the value and marks the key most recently used; putting an existing key updates its value and never evicts. Putting a new key into a full cache first evicts the least recently used key. With capacity 0 nothing is ever stored.
Output (stdout, one JSON object): {"results": [...]} with one entry per op: get gives its value or null, put gives null.

stages.name: cr1
stages.text: Change request 1: put now returns the key it evicted (a string), or null when nothing was evicted. With capacity 0, a put of a new key returns that same key (it is evicted immediately).

stages.name: cr2
stages.text: Change request 2: add a logical clock that starts at 0. New op ["tick", n: int >= 1] advances the clock by n and returns null. put may carry a 4th element ttl: int >= 1, so ["put", key, value, ttl]; the entry expires when clock >= (clock at put) + ttl. A put without ttl never expires; a put on an existing key replaces its ttl (or removes it when no ttl is given). An expired entry behaves as absent: get returns null. Before putting a new key into a full cache, all expired entries are removed first and are NOT reported as evicted; only if the cache is still full is the least recently used live key evicted and reported.

reqs.text: get returns value or null and refreshes recency
put on full cache evicts least recently used; update of existing key never evicts
put returns evicted key or null; capacity 0 returns own key
tick advances clock; entry expires at clock >= put time + ttl; put without ttl clears ttl
expired entries purged silently before LRU eviction
